assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work changed how economists and policymakers understand the distributional effects of technology and trade. It combines the task framework with the 'China shock' local-labour-market evidence, and it ties together measurement, causal design and policy relevance. It speaks directly to the question of how societies handle workers who lose out from structural change, which is a central concern of long-run economic history as well.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to the task-based and polarization literature. Autor, Dorn and Hanson jointly produced the China-shock evidence. Hanson also has earlier trade and geography contributions. Lawrence Katz is a major co-author of the earlier skill-biased change literature but is credited here with other work and is not proposed, because the three-person limit favours the China-shock trio.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of work, extensively replicated and debated. Its empirical core is mature, though the persistence and size of the trade effects are still contested.
uncertainties: Possible overlap in the committee's mind with recent prizes on labour-market causal methods and on technological change.
Debate over the long-run persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects.
Whether the task framework or the trade-shock evidence is the more prize-worthy core.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm model shifted trade theory from industry-level to firm-level analysis. It explains selection, exporter premia and new channels for gains from trade, and it reshaped both empirical and quantitative work. Trade has not been recognised since 2008, so the field is underrepresented relative to the importance of this contribution.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the foundational model. Helpman contributed heavily to the firm-heterogeneity agenda, including work with Melitz and Yeaple, and to the broader new trade theory. Redding is an important contributor but a third name seems less necessary.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of use, with a mature body of theory and firm-level evidence.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with Helpman's other candidate listing (B007), and the field's tendency to favour a Krugman-style pairing.
Whether Redding or other contributors such as Bernard and Jensen deserve inclusion.
Some of the empirical foundations (Bernard-Jensen exporter premia) are credited elsewhere.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint framework shows how small shocks are amplified through asset prices and credit. It underlies modern macro-finance and the understanding of credit cycles and crises, so its theoretical importance is high and long-standing.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 Kiyotaki-Moore paper is clearly the seminal contribution by these two. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator tradition, which is already partly recognised through the 2022 prize to Bernanke, so the proposal is limited to the two core originators.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years old, with abundant confirmation in subsequent macro-finance work and in the post-2008 literature.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Most of the evidence is a single paper plus the large literature it spawned.
The relative weight of Kiyotaki-Moore versus Bernanke-Gertler lines in committee thinking.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data brought new measurement of intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the geography of opportunity. This work resembles the historical-data approach of constructing new datasets and applying modern causal methods to them. It has had major influence on research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the agenda. Hendren is the main co-author on the neighbourhood and exposure-effect work. Friedman and Katz are significant collaborators but are not proposed, to keep the credit concentrated on the central originators. The co-author attribution is the hardest part.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade of high-impact work. Key results (the geography of mobility, exposure effects) are being replicated and refined, but long-run validation is still developing.
uncertainties: Timing: some of the findings are less than a decade old and are still being tested.
Credit division within a large team.
Chetty's wider contributions across public economics may be better judged as a separate entry (B042).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a way to measure how distortions across firms reduce aggregate productivity, and with it a quantitative account of cross-country income differences. It links micro data to macro development and has been applied widely, including in historical settings.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow's 2009 paper on China and India is the core contribution, and Klenow also worked on related productivity topics. Restuccia and Rogerson formalised the related theoretical framework, though Rogerson is not on this list. Restuccia is credited for the macro-development side but is not proposed.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of heavy use. It is mature, though measurement of misallocation has been questioned.
uncertainties: Concern that measured misallocation reflects measurement error or unobserved heterogeneity.
Questions about attribution to Restuccia, Rogerson and others.
Possible overlap with the recent growth-focused prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance literature has had a very large effect on how legal institutions are linked to financial development, and it provided new cross-country datasets. It is closely tied to the long-run institutions agenda that was recently recognised.
assessment.attribution: The LLSV core (La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, Vishny) is well defined. Vishny is a fourth name, and Shleifer has an extensive record in other areas such as behavioural finance. The three-person limit forces a choice that leaves out a real contributor.
assessment.maturity: Work dating from the late 1990s, with many follow-ups.
uncertainties: Serious critiques of the legal-origins hypothesis, including historical evidence that challenges the causal story.
Leaving out Vishny under the three-name limit.
Possible non-scientific controversies attached to one of the credited names, which I cannot assess from the supplied evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The long-run top-income series built from tax records transformed measurement of inequality and renewed a historical, data-driven approach in public debate and research. This is in the spirit of building new historical series, and it created the data infrastructure for the World Inequality Database.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez's 2003 top-incomes paper is the foundational study. Zucman extended the work to wealth and offshore holdings, with a more recent track record. The proposal focuses on the earlier two.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of work. The data are widely used, though methodological disputes about wealth estimation continue.
uncertainties: Methodological debates over the measurement of wealth and top shares, including the treatment of capital gains and pensions.
Whether the committee values the data contribution over theoretical or causal identification.
Saez also has an entry in B042, so credit may be split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a tractable non-cooperative foundation for bargaining and a link between bargaining and market outcomes. It is a standard tool across theory, labour, trade and industrial organisation.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the central contribution. Rubinstein and Wolinsky (1985) developed bargaining in decentralised markets. Binmore contributed to the strategic foundations and the interpretation of the Nash bargaining solution, and there are close antecedents (Stahl and others) that are not listed.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years old, with a very strong record of confirmation.
uncertainties: The game-theory field has received several recent awards, and this may weigh against a further one.
Binmore's contribution to bargaining is substantial and is left out of the proposal.
It is a theoretical contribution without major empirical confirmation of its own.
